source_name: OPSI — Pregled objavljenih pogodb po oddaji javnega naročila
why_relevant: Catalogue record for published post-award contracts (concessions and PPP included). Directly names counterparties to public contracts — the raw material for identifying payments/banking suppliers.

source_name: STATIST — analitična aplikacija o oddanih javnih naročilih (MJU / Direktorat za javno naročanje)
source_subtype: government analytics application with CSV export
why_relevant: Analytical front-end over all contracts awarded in Slovenia since 1 Jan 2013, filterable by supplier name, buyer, subject, legal basis, EU co-financing and value, with CSV export and daily refresh. Fast way to rank the top suppliers to Slovenian public bodies and to test whether a payments vendor holds recurring public contracts.

source_name: Statistično poročilo o oddanih javnih naročilih (MJU annual procurement statistics)
why_relevant: Annual official statistical report on awarded public contracts — gives market sizing, share by procedure type and category, useful for framing how large the addressable Slovenian public-sector spend is in IT/financial services.

source_name: AJPES — Poslovni register Slovenije (ePRS)
why_relevant: Authoritative company register: resolves a payee name harvested from ERAR/STATIST into a legal entity (matična številka, davčna številka, SKD activity code, address, ownership form). Essential normalisation layer before any vendor-level analysis, and the way to find related/subsidiary entities of payments vendors.

source_name: AJPES — JOLP: javno objavljena letna poročila
why_relevant: Free access to filed annual reports (last five years) for companies including banks, insurers and cooperatives. Lets you size a Slovenian payments/IT vendor's revenue and check whether public-contract income is material — the financial complement to the ERAR/STATIST payment trail.

source_name: AJPES — Register transakcijskih računov (eRTR)
why_relevant: National register of transaction accounts, linked to the business register, population register, tax register and beneficial-owner register. Relevant because it maps which entities bank where — a structural view of Slovenian bank-customer relationships and a cross-check on ERAR counterparty IBANs.

source_name: AJPES — Register dejanskih lastnikov (RDL)
why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership register under ZPPDFT-1. Useful for unmasking who actually stands behind a Slovenian payments/IT supplier or a bidding consortium. IMPORTANT ACCESS CHANGE: reported that as of 9 August 2025 amended legislation significantly narrowed who may access the register — access status must be re-checked before relying on it.

source_name: AJPES — Katalog informacij javnega značaja
why_relevant: AJPES's own catalogue of the public-information databases it holds. A meta-index: it enumerates every AJPES register/evidence, which is the reliable way to discover AJPES data assets beyond the well-known ePRS/JOLP/RTR trio.

source_name: Portal NIO — ERAR asset record (nacionalni interoperabilnostni okvir)
why_relevant: NIO is Slovenia's interoperability/asset catalogue for public-sector IT solutions. Beyond the ERAR record it indexes the software assets, data models and interoperability specs of Slovenian government systems — a secondary route to discovering which integrators build state financial IT.

source_name: Opentender Slovenia (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Third-party cleaned and standardised Slovenian procurement data with supplier/buyer analytics and integrity indicators. Useful as a cross-check and as an easier bulk source than scraping enarocanje.si, and it exposes cross-border comparability with other CEE markets.

source_name: OCP Data Registry — Slovenia (Ministry of Public Administration OCDS publication)
why_relevant: Registry entry describing Slovenia's OCDS-formatted procurement publication (via the They Buy For You platform). Tells you whether a standardised, machine-readable contracting feed exists, where it lives, and how current it is — the cheapest path to structured award/contract data.

source_name: Global Public Procurement Database (GPPD) — Slovenia country profile
why_relevant: World Bank-backed comparative profile of Slovenia's procurement system and data availability. Good for framing legal/institutional context and for validating what data is officially supposed to be published.

source_name: jnplacila.si — private-sector guidance and documentation on UJP JN Plačila reporting
why_relevant: Non-governmental site hosting UJP JN Plačila user documentation and practical guidance. Useful for understanding data field semantics, B2B interface options and reporting edge cases before building a collector — and it indicates a small ecosystem of SI ERP vendors (Vasco, SAOP iCenter, Minimax) that integrate with public payment reporting; those vendor sites are themselves downstream leads.

source_name: OPSI — Zbirka e-računov javnega sektorja (e-invoice collection, UJP)
why_relevant: Catalogue record for the collection of e-invoices that public-sector entities receive for payment (e-invoice envelopes, attachments; metadata available for download). E-invoice metadata is the most granular vendor-level spend signal available — finer than contract-level award data, and it directly names suppliers invoicing the state.

source_name: Portal javnih naročil (eNaročanje, Uradni list RS)
why_relevant: The statutory national publication point. SID banka's own procurement page explicitly states it publishes ALL javna naročila here / in Uradni list RS rather than on its own site, and the same applies to Kapitalska druzba. Filtering by naročnik (SID banka, ZZZS, ZPIZ, Posta Slovenije, Banka Slovenije, FURS/MF) gives contract notices and obvestila o oddaji naročila (award notices) with supplier names and values.

source_name: SID banka — Javna naročila (Informacije javnega značaja)
source_subtype: state bank transparency / procurement landing page
why_relevant: SID banka is a state-owned promotional/export bank and an obligated contracting entity; it buys core banking, treasury and IT systems. Fetched content shows the page hosts no notices itself but declares that all procurement goes to the Portal javnih naročil / Uradni list RS — valuable as a compliance-behaviour signal telling the collector where to look, and adjacent 'Javni pozivi' pages do carry own-site calls.

source_name: ZPIZ — Javna naročila (Zavod za pokojninsko in invalidsko zavarovanje)
why_relevant: ZPIZ disburses pensions to ~0.6m recipients — a very large recurring payment-processing and e-delivery buyer. Fetched page confirms three live sections: AKTUALNA JAVNA NAROČILA, Arhiv javnih naročil, Drugi javni razpisi, plus small-value procurements; visible example titles are IT-flavoured (e.g. a Gartner advisory membership), which is exactly the buying signal to track.

source_name: Pošta Slovenije — Javna naročila
why_relevant: Pošta Slovenije is a ZJN-3 sectoral contracting entity and a major payments-adjacent actor: it runs counter-based money services (denarne storitve v domačem prometu), cash logistics and post-office banking distribution. Its own page publishes both ZJN-3 tenders and non-binding 'javni pozivi za zbiranje informativnih ponudb', the latter being early-warning demand signals that never reach the national portal.

source_name: Kapitalska družba (KAD) — Javna naročila in oddaja nepremičnin
why_relevant: KAD manages the demographic reserve fund and pension-company assets (SKD 65.300); it buys asset-management, custody, reporting and IT services. Its page states that all javna naročila are published on the Portal javnih naročil, so it functions primarily as a routing pointer, while own-site PDFs carry javna zbiranja ponudb (e.g. asset/real-estate offers).

source_name: SDH — Slovenski državni holding, Aktualno / javni razpisi
why_relevant: SDH is the umbrella manager of state capital investments including banking and insurance stakes. Search evidence shows its published 'javni razpisi' are dominated by governance calls (management-board vacancies, supervisor accreditation) and by calls for binding offers to buy claims/assets — i.e. it is a weak IT/payments buyer but a strong signal source on ownership changes in banks and on divestment processes that reshape the buyer landscape.

source_name: ZZZS Portal za izvajalce — Razpisi (zdravstvene storitve)
source_subtype: payer supplier portal — calls for providers/suppliers
why_relevant: ZZZS is Slovenia's single health payer and one of the largest transaction originators in the country (contributions collection, provider reimbursements, the health insurance card system). Its supplier-facing portal carries the recurring razpisi; the card/e-services stack (kartica zdravstvenega zavarovanja, e-storitve) is the payments-adjacent asset base whose renewals surface here or on the national portal.

source_name: ZZZS corporate site (zzzs.si) — institutional / IJZ layer
source_subtype: institutional site, procurement section location unconfirmed
why_relevant: The corporate domain (with an /en/ mirror) is the expected home of ZZZS's own javna naročila / informacije javnega značaja section, distinct from the provider portal. Needed to catch general IT, payment-collection and card-issuance procurements that are not health-service razpisi.

source_name: FURS — Finančna uprava RS (fu.gov.si / gov.si)
source_subtype: tax authority site (buyer signals + payment scheme rules)
why_relevant: FURS collects all state duties and defines the payment rails taxpayers use (prescribed accounts, references, eDavki). It is not an independent contracting authority in its own right — it sits inside the Ministry of Finance, so its procurement is generally published under MF/gov.si and on the national portal. Its own pages are still the authoritative source for payment-reference and collection-scheme changes that drive supplier demand.
